source_text: φρόνιμος γίνου ὡς ὁ ὄφις ἐν ἅπασιν καὶ ἀκέραιος εἰς ἀεὶ ὡς ἡ περιστερά. διὰ τοῦτο σαρκικὸς εἶ καὶ πνευματικός, ἵνα τὰ φαινόμενά σου εἰς πρόσωπον κολακεύῃς· τὰ δὲ ἀόρατα αἴτει ἵνα σοι φανερωθῇ, ὅπως μηδενὸς λείπῃ καὶ παντὸς χαρίσματος περισσεύῃς.
pass_a_gloss: Be shrewd as the serpent in all things and forever innocent as the dove; for this you are fleshly and spiritual, to flatter what appears before the face; ask the unseen to be revealed, that you may lack nothing and abound in every charism.
pass_b_english: Be shrewd as the serpent in everything, and forever innocent as the dove. That is why you are both fleshly and spiritual: so you can deal gently with what shows before people’s faces, and ask for the unseen to be shown to you — that you may lack nothing and overflow with every gift.

choices.why: χάρισμα is the gifts-and-order hinge; bishop charged to abound in charism while holding office.
Ignatius pairs fleshly+spiritual ministry: visible pastoral tact + asking for unseen gifts.
rejected: flatter (empty praise as the main sense)

anf_compare.notes: Independent from ANF; sense matches serpent/dove + abound in every gift.

variants.note: TEI prints chapter marker '3,' mid-paragraph before ὁ καιρὸς; excerpt stops at περισσεύῃς (2.2 only).
